definition.name: Faith in a man over a prophecy (Neo)
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Whether to keep believing in a foretold savior or to transfer that belief to a fallible human being.
definition.summary: The crew's whole operation runs on Morpheus's certainty that a prophesied One will free humanity, so every event is read through that expectation (ev-012, ev-014). Neo's repeated failures—losing the sparring test (ev-015), falling short of the jump (ev-016), and his own insistence that he is not the One (ev-032)—strain that faith until Morpheus is captured precisely while protecting the man the crew still doubts (ev-025, ev-026, ev-031). The stance is finally tested and resolved not by prophecy being fulfilled but by Neo, self-denying, choosing to risk everything for Morpheus anyway (ev-032), surviving death (ev-044), and doing what no prophecy predicted—destroying an Agent (ev-045)—so belief is vindicated by a man who never claimed the title rather than by the title itself.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus is 'certain they have found the one' and rebuilds Neo's body; this installs the prophecy-expectation through which every later event in this plot is read.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: Establishes the founding certainty (faith in a foretold savior) that the rest of the plot strains and finally re-resolves.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo recoils from the crew as 'agents of an unbearable violation,' so the man being folded into a prophecy-faith physically resists the very believers—the first crack between belief and its human object.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-012: Because Morpheus has committed to Neo as the One (ev-012), Neo's revulsion at the crew who serve that belief stages the tension the plot tracks: faith pinned to a man who rejects it.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus recounts the Oracle's prophecy and declares 'the search is over' before Neo has proven anything—stating the stance at its strongest.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-013: Neo's resistance (ev-013) is answered not with doubt but with Morpheus doubling down on destiny, so the plot's faith reaches its peak just before the failures begin.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo loses the sparring test to Morpheus—the prophecy-certainty meeting its first concrete failure in the man it is pinned to.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-014: The 'search is over' declaration (ev-014) sets an expectation that the sparring loss (ev-015) directly undercuts, beginning the strain on belief-in-the-One.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo falls badly short of the jump while the crew watches 'split between doubters and believers,' directly staging whether faith in the foretold One can survive his repeated shortfalls.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-015: The sparring defeat (ev-015) escalates into a public, witnessed failure (ev-016), widening the crew's doubt/belief split and deepening the plot's central question.

chain.why_in_plot: Cypher recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count ('five before him took on an Agent and died'), openly challenging whether belief in the foretold One is warranted.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-016: The visible shortfall at the jump (ev-016) gives Cypher the grounds to reframe the prophecy as fatal delusion, voicing the plot's doubt at its bluntest.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus confesses he 'misunderstood the Oracle,' exposing that the certainty the whole operation runs on may rest on a misreading.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-020: Cypher's body-count challenge (ev-020) presses Neo to question the five failed candidates, which forces Morpheus's admission (ev-022) that the faith may be built on error.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus chooses to give his own life to save Neo—the man the crew still doubts—precisely because he believes in the prophecy, so faith now costs freedom.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-022: Even after confessing possible misreading (ev-022), Morpheus acts on the belief anyway, sacrificing himself for the doubted man, converting abstract faith into a fatal wager.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus is captured while protecting the doubted man; the faith-driven sacrifice produces the plot's central crisis.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-025: Morpheus's self-sacrifice to save Neo (ev-025) leaves him exposed and taken, so the cost of believing in the One becomes a concrete captivity to be answered.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus is interrogated to the breaking point rather than betray the man he champions, pushing the stance to its limit.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-026: The capture (ev-026) delivers Morpheus to the Agents, whose escalating interrogation (ev-031) tests whether faith in the One can survive his destruction.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo denies being the One yet commits to rescuing Morpheus anyway, converting the mission from prophecy into a wager on a man—the stance pivots from title to person.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-031: Morpheus nearing the breaking point (ev-031) forces Neo to choose; his self-denial plus his rescue decision transfers belief from the foretold title to a fallible human being.

chain.why_in_plot: After the rescue, Morpheus reinterprets both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation, forcing events back through the lens of belief even as Neo tries to report a contrary verdict.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-032: Neo's man-over-prophecy rescue (ev-032) succeeds, but Morpheus re-absorbs the outcome into prophecy-language, showing the stance's pull even after the pivot.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus reads Neo's stillness before the fight as 'the beginning of belief,' continuing to translate the man's actions into prophecy-terms.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-035: Having reasserted the prophetic frame (ev-035), Morpheus keeps reading Neo's behavior as confirmation of the One, sustaining the tension between title and person into the climax.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo survives death and the life monitors jump back to life—a miracle that exceeds what the doctrine predicted and begins to vindicate belief through the man rather than the title.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-038: Neo's choice to stand and fight (ev-038) leads to his death at the Agents' hands, and his return (ev-044) is a resurrection no prophecy mapped—belief vindicated by the person.

chain.why_in_plot: Neo destroys Agent Smith—an act 'no prophecy predicted'—so belief is finally vindicated by a man who never claimed the title rather than by the title itself, closing the stance.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-044: The resurrection (ev-044) empowers Neo to do what the foretold-One doctrine never forecast—kill an Agent—resolving the plot by proving faith in the man, not the prophecy.

definition.name: From deferential compliance to self-authored conviction (Neo)
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Whether to let external authority define who you are or to author your own identity through choice.
definition.summary: Neo begins as a man split between two lives and governed by others' definitions—answering to a boss's ultimatum with flat compliance (ev-005), accepting an arrest he knows he can break (ev-001's world), and letting Morpheus's 'the One' label land on him before he has chosen it (ev-008, ev-010). As he is dismantled and rebuilt, he resists the truth physically (ev-013) and keeps measuring himself against a role he did not pick (ev-015, ev-016). His stance is tested when he refuses both Smith's erasure (ev-007) and Cypher's cynical reading of the prophecy (ev-020), and is resolved only when he stops accepting any verdict—Smith's death sentence (ev-039) and the crew's death monitors (ev-044)—and acts from a conviction no one handed him, walking out of the phone booth under his own power (ev-047).

chain.why_in_plot: Sets the baseline of the plot: when Rhineheart delivers an either-or ultimatum about his job, Neo answers with flat, deferential compliance, letting an external authority dictate his position rather than authoring one (sc-016).
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: No earlier member event; this is the plot's starting state of governed-by-others that every later event departs from.

chain.why_in_plot: First crack in that compliance: Smith lays out Neo's two lives and offers to erase his record, and Neo—still the man who obeys bosses—refuses with contempt and demands his phone call, an authority's offer/definition rejected rather than accepted (sc-020).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-005: Because ev-005 establishes Neo as one who answers authority with deferential compliance, his contemptuous refusal of Smith's offer in ev-007 reads as the first deviation from that baseline—the same pressure that produced compliance now producing a refusal, which is what makes it a turn.

chain.why_in_plot: Shows the refusal is not yet self-authorship: a voice names him 'the One' and demands a 'Yes,' and Neo walks to the bridge and gets into the car without having chosen the label—letting an external authority's designation land on him before he has authored it (sc-022, sc-023).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-007: Ev-007 ends with Neo's mouth sealed by Smith's power, leaving him unable to speak for himself; that silencing carries directly into ev-008, where a voice speaks for him ('the One') and he submits to being taken (gunpoint, 'for our protection. chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-008: Ev-008 delivers Neo, unconsulted, into the crew's custody (the car, the gun, the 'our way' that is not his); ev-010 is the next step of that same handover—Trinity brings him to room 1313 and hands him to Morpheus, who sets the terms of the choice Neo then makes, so the extraction of ev-008 enables

chain.why_in_plot: The handed-down framework is now forced on his body: Morpheus walks him through the truth that humans are farmed for power, and Neo resists every step, recoiling from the crew's touch—physically resisting a reality an authority is imposing that he has not made his own (sc-040, sc-043).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-010: The red pill Neo swallows in ev-010 is what unhooks him from the simulation and delivers him to the Nebuchadnezzar; that same act of accepting Morpheus's terms produces the consequence he did not bargain for in ev-013, where Morpheus forces the truth of that system onto him and his body rejects it.

chain.why_in_plot: Even as he is rebuilt, he measures himself against a role he hasn't owned: after downloading kung fu he comes out convinced he knows how to fight, and Morpheus dismantles that claim in the dojo—Neo still judging himself by an ability handed to him rather than genuinely made his own (sc-049, sc-055).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-013: Ev-013 strips Neo of the false reality he had accepted from others, leaving him with no borrowed identity to lean on; that cleared ground is what makes the rebuild of ev-015 necessary and possible—Morpheus now downloads skill into the emptied-out Neo, who then mistakenly treats the downloaded role

chain.why_in_plot: The role's demand still exceeds him: in the rooftop jump program he runs and falls badly short, spitting blood—still failing against a test defined by others, unable yet to author the belief the role requires (sc-059, sc-060).

chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-016: Ev-016 leaves Neo failing a belief-test he cannot yet pass, exposed and uncertain about his place in the role; that shaken uncertainty is exactly the opening Cypher exploits in ev-020, recasting the prophecy as a death sentence to convert him—and Neo's refusal to be converted only makes sense again

chain.why_in_plot: An outright rejection of an authority's pronouncement of his end: Smith uses the arriving train to frame Neo's death as settled inevitability, and at the edge of death Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces, summoning a surge from within (sc-182, sc-184).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-032: Ev-032 establishes that Neo can act from inside—staking a rescue on a belief no one handed him and denying the 'One' verdict rather than accepting it; that newly proven capacity to author his own move is what he draws on in ev-039, where instead of accepting the death Smith pronounces he refuses it

chain.why_in_plot: He stops accepting the final external verdict: in the real world the life monitors flatline and the crew gives him up, but Neo returns to life—no longer bound by the death sentence the crew's instruments (an external authority) pronounce (sc-209, sc-213).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-039: Ev-039 is Neo's first refusal of an authority's death pronouncement (Smith's), summoning a surge from within at the edge of death; ev-044 escalates that same refusal to its limit—when the crew's monitors pronounce him dead and they give him up, he does not accept that verdict either and returns, co

chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-044: Ev-044 is the moment Neo stops accepting any externally pronounced ending and returns to life on his own; that completed break from every external verdict—boss, Agent, prophecy, crew monitors—leaves him free in ev-047 to act purely from within, rising into flight under his own power rather than run

definition.name: Certainty that must survive its own disillusionment (Morpheus)
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Whether unshakeable belief is strength or a dangerous delusion that gets people killed.
definition.summary: Morpheus carries an absolute faith that reframes rescue as destiny and declares 'the search is over' before Neo has proven anything (ev-014), and he presses that certainty onto the crew and onto Neo through training and prophecy (ev-015, ev-016, ev-022). This stance is tested when his own confession reveals he misunderstood the Oracle and his belief has already produced a body count (ev-022, ev-020), and again when that same faith costs him his freedom as he sacrifices himself for the man he champions (ev-025, ev-026, ev-031). His certainty is resolved not by being proven right about the prophecy but by being forced to reinterpret events through Neo's self-denial (ev-035) and finally witnessing a miracle that exceeds what his doctrine predicted (ev-044, ev-045), leaving his faith intact but changed by what it survived.

chain.why_in_plot: The founding act of the certainty the plot tracks: Morpheus reframes a rescue as destiny and declares 'the search is over' before Neo has proven anything (sc-045, sc-046).
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: Establishes the absolute faith that every later event either presses, tests, or forces to survive.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus refuses to celebrate Neo's downloaded skill and instead submits it to a physical test, pressing his certainty onto Neo through training rather than accepting the claim at face value (sc-048, sc-049).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-014: Having declared the search over, Morpheus must now make Neo into what he has already proclaimed him to be, so he meets the download not with celebration but with the dojo test.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus stages the rooftop jump to prove the mind governs reality, imposing his faith-driven model of the Construct on Neo after Neo falls short (sc-058, sc-059).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-015: The sparring defeat shows Neo still bound by technique and physics, so Morpheus escalates to the jump program to enforce the faith-based physics his certainty requires.

chain.why_in_plot: During the ascent to the Oracle, Morpheus confesses he misunderstood the Oracle—his certainty cracking under the admission that his belief has already produced a body count (sc-080, sc-081).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-016: The failed jump and Neo's doubt press Morpheus toward the Oracle, where the very certainty that drove the training forces the confession that it was built on a misunderstanding.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus chooses to give his own life so Neo can escape—the same faith that champions the man he believes is the One now costing him his freedom (sc-115, sc-116).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-022: The disillusioned confession does not break his faith but redirects it into action: having admitted the cost of his belief, he now willingly pays it by staking his life on the man he still champions.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus is captured while dominant over Smith, the faith-driven sacrifice of ev-025 completing in the loss of his freedom (sc-123).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-025: The choice to trade his life for Neo's escape places him in the room with Smith, where the sacrifice he chose resolves into his actual capture.

chain.why_in_plot: Under a doubled serum dosage, Morpheus spends his last agency fighting to keep his mind from cracking rather than yielding—the certainty tested to the point of breaking by the very faith that put him there (sc-145).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-026: The capture delivers him into Smith's hands, so the freedom his faith cost him is now pressed to its limit as the interrogation drives his certainty to the edge of breaking.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus cuts Neo off and reinterprets both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation, forcing events to fit his doctrine even as Neo's self-denial should undermine it (sc-170).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-031: Having survived the serum without yielding, Morpheus emerges with his faith hardened rather than dissolved, so he meets Neo's doubt by reasserting the doctrine instead of conceding to it.

chain.why_in_plot: Watching Neo stand to fight, Morpheus reads that stillness as the beginning of belief—reinterpreting Neo's self-authored choice through the lens of his own certainty (sc-179, sc-180).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-035: Having already reinterpreted Neo's self-denial as confirmation, Morpheus now reads Neo's decision to stand and fight through the same lens, converting a self-authored choice into evidence for his faith.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus, who had reached for the EMP in weeping despair, witnesses Neo's monitors jump back to life—a miracle that exceeds what his doctrine predicted and forces his faith to survive its own disillusionment (sc-209, sc-210).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-038: The reinterpretation that sustained his certainty through Neo's doubt now faces the ultimate test—Neo's death—where his doctrine has no answer, and the return to life forces his faith to endure something it never foretold.

chain.why_in_plot: Morpheus declares Neo the One as Neo destroys an Agent—witnessing a miracle that surpasses his prophecy, leaving his faith intact but changed by what it survived (sc-216, sc-217).
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-044: The miracle of Neo's return completes in a feat beyond any prediction, so Morpheus's declaration is no longer the premature certainty of ev-014 but a faith confirmed by something his doctrine could not have contained.

definition.name: Trust forged through doubt into devotion (Neo and Trinity)
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Whether intimacy built on guarded suspicion can become a bond worth dying for.
definition.summary: The bond begins as enforced mistrust—Trinity held at gunpoint from Neo the moment he wakes and insisting the restraint is 'for our protection from you' (ev-008)—then moves through wary honesty on the way to the Oracle (ev-021) and a private, unownable closeness that Trinity shields from Cypher's needling (ev-017). The stance is tested when Trinity, gutted by Morpheus's condition and Neo's self-doubt, converts grief into command and commits to the rescue anyway (ev-032), and is resolved when she alone refuses to accept Neo's death, reviving him with a kiss (ev-044), and when the man who once had to be restrained now breaks free of her embrace only to send her to safety first (ev-030) before his final act is reached for her voice (ev-047).

chain.why_in_plot: Seeds the bond at its coldest: Trinity holds Neo at gunpoint from the instant he wakes and frames the restraint as 'for our protection. From you,' establishing enforced mistrust as the relationship's starting stance.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: Provides the stance the rest of the plot will reverse — the gun and the 'From you' framing are the guarded suspicion that later devotion answers, so it must stand first.

chain.why_in_plot: Moves the bond past suspicion into a private, unownable closeness — Trinity emerges from being alone with the unconscious Neo and shields that intimacy from Cypher's needling, guarding a feeling she cannot yet name.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-008: The enforced-restraint stance of ev-008 (Neo dangerous, to be held at gunpoint) is what makes the turn meaningful: Trinity is alone with the man she was told to fear, and instead of guarding against him she guards a tenderness for him — the suspicion begins converting to feeling.

chain.why_in_plot: Advances the guarded intimacy toward wary honesty as Neo presses Trinity about what the Oracle told her on the way to the meeting, deepening trust through shared vulnerability rather than orders.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-017: ev-017 establishes a closeness Trinity can feel but not yet speak (she shields it from Cypher); ev-021 is the first place that unspoken feeling is tested in the open, as Neo presses her into honest exchange on the drive — the private closeness becomes shared, spoken trust.

chain.why_in_plot: Reverses the opening stance: the man who had to be restrained now breaks free of Trinity's embrace only to send her to safety first, proving the mistrust has become mutual devotion.

definition.name: A system that preserves itself by harvesting and betraying its own (the Matrix / the crew's world)
definition.theme_or_dilemma: Whether an order maintained by control and consumption can be resisted from within without being reproduced.
definition.summary: The dominant system is introduced as a seamless order that farms humans for power and erases dissenters' minds (ev-011, ev-013), and enforces itself through Agents who can occupy anyone still hardwired to it (ev-018) and through citizens who police the rebels (ev-001, ev-003). The system's logic is mirrored inside the resistance when Cypher, disgusted by the cost of freedom, bargains to be reinserted and feeds Morpheus to the very power he fled (ev-020, ev-026, ev-029), so the threat of assimilation comes from within. The stance is tested as the system nearly succeeds—capturing its most dangerous mind (ev-031), killing the crew's members (ev-029, ev-030), and cornering the ship with Sentinels (ev-040, ev-042, ev-044)—and is resolved when a freed human enters an Agent and destroys it from inside (ev-045), breaking the system's rule that no one escapes or fights back, even as the survivors must still flee its counterstrike (ev-046).

chain.why_in_plot: setup: the dominant order is introduced as one that survives by turning its own people into its enforcers — the cops breach and take Trinity, while Agent Smith corrects the Lieutenant's belief that the raid is succeeding, showing the system correcting itself through the humans plugged into it.
chain.caused_by_previous: Opens the chain: OPENING establishes the system as the plot's antagonist; this event instantiates its first rule, that it polices itself through occupied citizens, so every later betrayal and enforcement is measured against this seamless self-correction.

chain.why_in_plot: setup: the system's reach is shown total and adaptive — Agents block the alley, match her leap, and close every route — establishing the seamless enforcement the whole plot is measured against.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-001: Because the raid in ev-001 failed to hold Trinity, the same occupying force (Agents Brown and Smith) pursues her across the rooftops, demonstrating that the order closes every escape the way it corrected the cops' belief.

chain.why_in_plot: turn: the system's self-preservation is shown to include erasing dissenters from within — Smith offers to wipe Neo's record clean, and when refused, seals his mouth and implants a tracker, the order reproducing itself inside the body it cannot otherwise persuade.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-003: Having shown in ev-003 that open pursuit can be slipped (Trinity reaches a phone), the system shifts to the quieter method of occupying and marking a dissenter from inside, so the same enforcement that failed on the rooftops now succeeds silently in the interrogation room.

chain.why_in_plot: turn: the system's core logic — farming humans for power — is exposed as the material basis of the order, and Neo's harvest-and-flush treatment (severing the cables, vacuuming him into the waste line) shows how it disposes of its own.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-007: The tracker implanted in ev-007 lets the system locate and harvest Neo's real body, so the interrogation's failed persuasion resolves into the physical act of severing him from the power source he was feeding.

chain.why_in_plot: turn: the harvesting order is named and its violation made visceral; Neo recoils from the crew as 'agents of an unbearable violation,' showing how the system's consumption reshapes even the freed — the cost the rest of the plot must reckon with.
chain.caused_by_previous: enabled by ev-011: Because Neo was just farmed and flushed by the very order that grew him (ev-011), the naming of that order on the Nebuchadnezzar lands as violation rather than liberation, so the material harvest produces the psychological recoil that defines the cost of resisting from within.

chain.why_in_plot: turn: the system's enforcement mechanism is defined — Agents are sentient programs that can occupy anyone still hardwired to it, so the order reproduces itself through the very people it is plugged into, the rule Neo will finally break.
